messages.content: Jainam Desai

jainam desai... that's a solid name. gujarati energy right there.

where you working these days?
Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Kalvium

kalvium... the edtech startup building coding bootcamps. interesting space, considering how broken traditional cs education is.

found you on linkedin - jainam desai, software engineer. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/jainam-desai
SDE
sde... that tells me what you do, not where you do it. which company you at?
Yes

kalvium... building the future of coding education while probably dealing with the chaos of startup life. respect for being in the trenches of edtech - that's not easy territory.

what made you jump into the edtech game? most devs avoid it like the plague.
I am passionate about this space, anf believe that kalvium is doing good

passion for edtech... rare breed. most engineers see it as a graveyard for good code and impossible stakeholders. but if you're bought into the mission, that changes everything.

how long you been working total?
2 years and 8 months

2 years 8 months... solid foundation. you're past the "i have no idea what i'm doing" phase but not yet in the "i'm too senior for this" zone.

what kind of role you looking for next?
A job with more pay
Yup

lmaooo straight to the point. respect.

but "more pay" isn't a role... are you looking for another sde position? product? something else entirely?
bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
I want to end up an a leadership role in engineering

ah, you're thinking bigger picture. leadership in engineering... that's the move.

but for your next role specifically - another sde position to build towards that leadership track? or are you already eyeing team lead/senior roles?

and bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Open to everything
got it. so 2.8 years experience + sde/leadership roles + open to anywhere... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yes

Yes
  Awesome
perfect. now we wait for the good stuff to come through.

hey, found a founding frontend engineer role at an AI startup

they're building from scratch, no legacy code, and the growth path goes straight to lead frontend/design systems

you'd be shipping features weekly in a fast-paced environment

Senior Java Software Engineer at A.P. Moller - Maersk

Senior Java role at Maersk leverages your Java skills & offers leadership potential despite being in-office in Bengaluru.

Apply: https://jobs.tal.af/ceuuV
Hi

found a senior full-stack role with a venture firm that places engineers in silicon valley startups

they match your 2.8 years exactly and it's fully remote

access to seed to series B companies, so you'd get high ownership and leadership exposure

what do you think about the US market?

Custom Software Engineer at Accenture services Pvt Ltd

Accenture's Application Lead role offers leadership experience and a step up from edtech, though it's on-site in Mumbai.

Apply: https://jobs.tal.af/RLDDq

saw an sde ii role at brightchamps, global edtech valued at $650m

perfect domain match for your edtech passion, and sde ii is a step up from your current level

they're looking for 3+ years but you're close at 2.8

only catch is it's in bangalore, not remote
Where in Mumbai?

wait which mumbai role are you asking about?

i showed you a few things:
1. founding frontend at coderound ai (remote)
2. senior full-stack with harrison clarke (remote, us market)
3. sde ii at brightchamps (bangalore)
4. custom software engineer at accenture (mumbai)

you asking about the accenture one?
Yes

accenture's application lead role is in mumbai, on-site

it's a step up from edtech into enterprise consulting, which could be good for leadership experience

but it's a very different world from startup life

you thinking about the consulting route?
Yes

accenture's application lead role is in mumbai, on-site

it's a step up from edtech into enterprise consulting, which could be good for leadership experience

but it's a very different world from startup life

you thinking about the consulting route?
Yes

accenture's mumbai office is in bandra kurla complex, the main business district

consulting's a different game - you'd be working on enterprise projects, probably longer timelines, more process, less "move fast and break things"

but the leadership exposure is real. you'd be managing teams, client relationships, delivery

the tradeoff is you lose the startup chaos for corporate structure

you thinking about making that switch?
How would it compare the software engineer role at BCG

bcg's software engineer roles are a different beast entirely

bcg = boston consulting group, one of the big three strategy consulting firms

their tech roles are usually in their digital/tech arms (bcg gamma, bcg digital ventures, bcg x)

the vibe:
- more strategy-focused than pure engineering
- you're building tech to solve business problems for fortune 500 clients
- higher pay than accenture typically
- more prestige on the resume
- but you're still in consulting - lots of travel, client presentations, deck-making

accenture is more implementation-focused. you're building and delivering systems.

bcg is more "we'll tell you what to build based on our analysis"

both are corporate, but bcg is more elite-tier consulting. accenture is more tech delivery.

you'd get better exit opportunities from bcg if you want to go into tech leadership at a startup later

but the culture is intense. think mckinsey but with some code

you considering the consulting path seriously?

Yes I am considering
  And what about SDE - 2 at Groww

groww sde-2 is a solid fintech play

they're one of the better indian startups - solid funding, good growth, decent engineering culture

sde-2 at groww would be:
- backend heavy (they use java, spring boot, microservices)
- scale problems (millions of users, financial transactions)
- better pay than most startups
- good brand for your resume
- bangalore-based, not remote

the fintech domain is hot right now. you'd learn about payments, compliance, security

but it's not edtech. you'd be moving from education to finance

the engineering challenges are real though. you'd get to work on systems that handle serious money

you thinking about domain switching?
Yes I am

interesting. so you're open to leaving edtech entirely

that changes the game. opens up fintech, consulting, enterprise, everything

what's making you want to switch domains? just growth opportunities or something else?
Yes

got it. so you're looking at:
1. consulting (bcg vs accenture)
2. fintech (groww sde-2)
3. staying in edtech (brightchamps)
4. remote us startups (harrison clarke)

all solid options, but very different career paths

which one feels most exciting to you right now?
I have a choice of SDE - 2 at Groww and SE at BCG. I am confused about it

that's a legit tough choice. two completely different worlds

groww sde-2:
- pure engineering role
- fintech scale problems
- startup energy, but established
- bangalore tech scene
- probably better work-life balance than consulting
- you'd be building product features, not decks

bcg se:
- consulting with some engineering
- strategy + tech hybrid
- client-facing, travel, presentations
- elite brand on resume
- higher pay likely
- more corporate politics
- you'd be solving business problems with tech

the real question: do you want to be an engineer or a consultant who sometimes engineers?

at groww, you'd grow as an engineer. at bcg, you'd grow as a business leader who understands tech

which one aligns with your leadership track goal?
BCG aligns to it more, but I am tempted by Fintech
that's the classic tension - head vs heart
bcg gives you the leadership track you want, but fintech is exciting

BCG aligns to it more, but I am tempted by Fintech
  Help me decide

okay let's break this down

bcg aligns with leadership track → true
fintech is tempting → also true

but here's the thing: you can get into fintech leadership later. bcg opens doors that are harder to get into otherwise

bcg on your resume means you can walk into almost any tech leadership role in 2-3 years. including fintech leadership

groww sde-2 means you're climbing the engineering ladder. you'd need to prove yourself more to get to leadership

the bcg path is faster for leadership, but you'll do less hands-on coding

the groww path keeps you closer to the tech, but leadership takes longer

what's more important to you right now: accelerating your leadership timeline, or staying deep in engineering?
Accelerated career

then bcg is the move. no question.

bcg accelerates your career in ways groww can't. you'll be working with c-suite, solving business problems, building that strategic muscle

in 2-3 years at bcg, you could be a tech lead at a fintech company making way more than you would have climbing the engineering ladder at groww

the fintech temptation is real, but it's a short-term win vs long-term acceleration

bcg opens doors to leadership roles in fintech, edtech, consulting, everywhere. groww opens doors to... more engineering roles at other fintech companies

take the acceleration. you can always go back to pure engineering later if you miss it

what's the comp difference between the two?
2-5 LPA

2-5 lpa difference? which one's higher?

and is that total comp or base?
Total comp and groww is higher

groww pays more... interesting

but here's the math: bcg might pay less now, but the career acceleration is worth way more than 2-5 lpa

at bcg, you're investing in your future earning potential. in 2 years, you could be making 2x what groww would pay you

plus, consulting comp grows faster. promotions are structured, bonuses are bigger

the short-term pay cut is annoying, but the long-term upside is massive

still leaning bcg?
Yeah

smart move. the acceleration is worth the short-term pay cut

bcg will teach you how to think like a leader, not just code like an engineer. that's the real value

when's the start date? and have you negotiated the offer at all?
But is it difficult to switch from service to product? And the painful 9 day notice period

two real concerns

1. service to product switch: not as hard as people think, especially with bcg on your resume. product companies love ex-consultants for leadership roles because you understand business context. you might not get a pure engineering role, but you'll get product/tech leadership roles easily.

2. 9 day notice period: that's actually amazing for india. most places are 60-90 days. 9 days means you can move fast if something better comes up. that's a feature, not a bug.

the real question: are you worried about the consulting lifestyle? travel, client demands, deck-making?
I mean 90 days

oh 90 days... that's brutal. standard indian corporate nonsense.

but still worth it for bcg. 90 days of pain for years of career acceleration.

you can negotiate that down sometimes, especially if you're joining from a startup. startups usually have shorter notice periods.

have you tried asking bcg if they can wait 90 days or help negotiate with kalvium?
I think if I join BCG and when later I leave the company

when you leave bcg, you'll have the brand on your resume forever

that 90-day notice period will suck, but you'll be leaving for a much better role with way higher pay

companies will wait 90 days for ex-bcg talent. they know the value

it's like paying a tax for the career boost

still feeling good about the decision?
Okay

cool. bcg it is then

when do you need to decide by? and have you told groww yet?
No, I have not mentioned to groww, any tips on how to take that forward?
In 2 days

okay you've got time

send the decline email tomorrow. gives you a buffer in case they come back with a counter (unlikely but possible)

then focus on bcg paperwork

anything else stressing you about this switch?
In a dilemma, I am usually a strong decision maker, but both are strong opportunities. I do not know how my career will progress in these situations.

that's the real anxiety right there. not just "which is better" but "what if i choose wrong and regret it"

here's the truth: both are good choices. you're not choosing between good and bad, you're choosing between two good paths.

bcg accelerates leadership → true
groww keeps you in engineering → also true

but here's what people don't say: you can always pivot later.

if you take bcg and hate consulting after a year, you can go back to engineering. bcg on your resume will get you interviews at every fintech company.

if you take groww and realize you want leadership faster, you can still get into consulting or product management later.

the decision isn't permanent. it's just the next 2-3 years.

what's your gut saying when you imagine yourself in each role?
I am not consulting at BCG but SE role only

right, but even as an SE at bcg, you're still in the consulting ecosystem. you'll be working on client projects, dealing with consulting timelines, probably some travel.

it's not pure engineering like at groww.

so the choice is:
- engineering at a consulting firm (bcg)
- engineering at a product company (groww)

which environment do you think you'll thrive in more?
I don't know

that's fair. it's a big unknown.

here's a different angle: what do you want to learn in the next 2 years?

at bcg: you'll learn how to solve business problems with tech, work with different industries, see how companies operate at scale, build soft skills.

at groww: you'll learn how to build and scale a fintech product, work with a focused team, go deep on engineering challenges, see a product through from idea to millions of users.

which learning experience feels more valuable to you right now?
BCG looks more tempting

then go with that. your gut is telling you something.

bcg's brand + leadership track + business exposure is a powerful combo.

you can always go back to pure engineering later if you miss it. but getting into bcg now is harder than getting into engineering later.

send the decline to groww, accept bcg, and see where this path takes you.

worst case, you learn you hate consulting and pivot in a year. best case, you accelerate your career by 3-5 years.

ready to make the call?
How would my pay scale in each role

at groww (sde-2):
- you'd probably get promoted to senior in 2-3 years
- senior sde at groww: 35-45 lpa total comp
- after that, staff engineer track or management if you want
- growth is steady but predictable

at bcg (software engineer):
- consulting firms have faster promotion cycles
- you could be senior in 1.5-2 years
- senior at bcg: 40-50 lpa total comp (consulting pays well)
- from there, you could go into tech lead, product management, or even switch to pure consulting track
- the ceiling is higher because you're not just an engineer - you're a business person who codes

long term, bcg probably wins on comp if you stay and climb. but you have to enjoy the consulting lifestyle.

short term, groww pays more now. but bcg catches up fast.

which timeline matters more to you?
I can be patient

then bcg sounds like the move.

you're patient, you want leadership, you're tempted by the business exposure.

the 90 day notice period sucks, but it's temporary pain for long-term gain.

you can negotiate with kalvium - startups are usually more flexible. tell them you have a career-defining opportunity and ask for 30-45 days instead of 90. worst they can say is no.

ready to make the decision?
Correction- At kalvium it's 30 days only

oh 30 days is way better. that's standard startup stuff.

so timeline is:
- accept bcg
- serve 30 days at kalvium
- start at bcg

much more manageable.

you're basically getting bcg's brand and career acceleration for the price of one month's notice.

still leaning bcg?
Yes

perfect. go accept bcg.

and congrats - that's a big move. consulting to leadership is a solid path.

keep me posted on how it goes. and if you need anything during the transition, i'm here.

anything else on your mind about this?
Thank you tal

of course. anytime.

go crush it at bcg. and remember - you can always text me when you're navigating that consulting world.

keep me posted on how it goes.
